rel.body:
## v1.1.8 — hotfix for "Failed to get an adapter supporting Direct3D 12" (issue #29)

**v1.1.8 is v1.1.7 plus one fix.** If v1.1.7 starts fine for you, v1.1.8 changes nothing you can see; if it refused to start, this is the release you need.

### 🩹 What was wrong

The v1.1.7 `downpour.exe` exported a DirectX **Agility SDK** requirement (`D3D12SDKVersion` / `D3D12SDKPath`) — a leftover from the retired native-render debugging work — but the package never shipped the Agility runtime (`D3D12\D3D12Core.dll`). Windows 11 24H2 and newer ignore that because their inbox Direct3D 12 runtime is already recent enough, which is why the release tested clean on the build machine. On **Windows 10 and older Windows 11 builds** the loader insists on the missing file, every D3D12 device creation fails, and the game dies at boot with:

```

rel.body:
# ZOE Recompiled Version 1.1.0 Patch Notes:

In 1.0, a PC that could not finish every frame in time slowed the whole game down: slow motion and crackling sound.
From this version the game and its sound stay at full speed, and a PC that falls behind shows fewer frames instead.

The game also needs less CPU than before.

### What's new
- **The game should no longer run in slow motion on slower PCs.** When a frame is late, the next one is skipped and the
  game catches up. Controls, physics and music keep their normal speed.
- **Clean sound on slower PCs.** The crackling came from the slowdown and is gone with it.
- **Less CPU work per frame.** The game's sound driver now runs as native code, and the timing code was trimmed.

#### What runs as native PC code
- **The game's own program** (all 37,386 functions of game logic, AI, physics, menus): translated from PS2
  machine code to C++ and compiled for your CPU. Since 1.0.
- **The vector-unit programs** that build the 3D geometry and particles: compiled ahead of time. Since 1.0.
- **The sound driver**, Konami's own code that sequences the music and sound effects: compiled ahead of
  time. New in 1.1.0; it was interpreted one instruction at a time before.
- **Drawing**: the PS2's graphics commands are drawn by your graphics card through OpenGL.

### What is still modelled in software
- **The sound chip** that mixes the 48 voices into the audio you hear.
- **The graphics chip's rules** (how PS2 drawing commands are interpreted before they reach your graphics card).
- **PS2 timing**: the scheduler that keeps the game, sound and video in step.

These three are why a fast CPU still helps, and they are what we are working on next.

rel.body:
## v0.2.2.1 — Windows and Linux performance update

A performance update for **Windows** and **Linux** (the Steam Deck included), from a rework of how the game
is recompiled and drawn. Android and PS5 are unchanged in this release: use v0.2.2 for Android (its
optimisation is still in progress) and v0.2.1 for the PS5.

> [!NOTE]
> **A black screen for a few seconds after START GAME is normal.** When you start the game from the hub,
> the screen can stay black for some seconds before the game appears: wait for it, it is not a crash.

**Recompiler**
- The game's memory reads and writes are now ordinary ones the C++ compiler can optimise (before, every
  one was forced to happen exactly as written), with the waits between threads kept correct.
- The recompiler finds the game's busy-wait loops (41 of them, the main loop's wait for the render thread
  among them) and makes them pause, then let other threads run, instead of spinning flat out. They do not
  sleep: a sleep woke too late for the game's handoffs between its threads, so frames missed the screen's
  refresh and 60 fps looked like 30.
- Linux: calls between the game's functions are direct calls again (a "large code model" setting had made
  every one an indirect call).
- Linux: timed waits no longer spin through their last millisecond.
- Direct3D's copies of its state into a command stream that the renderer never reads are skipped.

**Renderer**
- The game's shaders are built into the program, as on Android and the PS5: no shader build at the first
  start, and no `dxcompiler.dll` / DXC libraries in the release.
- The game's shaders read its memory and constants without 64-bit addresses, as plain uniform and storage
  buffers — lighter for the GPU (the Steam Deck's 3D scene pass went from 5–17 ms to about 3–4 ms).
- Strip index lists are kept in ordinary memory (no slow reads back from GPU-shared memory).
- The game's index buffers are drawn as Vulkan index buffers, so the GPU reuses transformed vertices.

## PS5: controller rumble works on a DualSense (#28, #29)

**What was wrong.** A DualSense starts in its advanced vibration mode, where the game's two rumble levels move nothing, so crashes, collisions and nitro never vibrated the pad.

**The fix.** The pad is now put in compatible mode once it is opened, so it rumbles from the game's levels like a DualShock 4. Nothing to turn on.

mcla_pad_haptics = true
mcla_adaptive_triggers = true
```

- **Haptics:** the pad's actuators play the low end of the game's sound plus its rumble, with extra feel from the car itself: road texture that grows with speed, a thump on each gear change, a knock on crashes and a surge while nitro burns.
- **Adaptive triggers:** resistance on R2 (throttle) and L2 (brake), short buzzes on wheelspin, hard braking and hits, a buzz near the top of each gear, and slack triggers in menus and the pause menu.

Tuning options (`mcla_haptics_*`, `mcla_trigger_*`) are listed in `ps5/game/ps5_haptics.h` and `ps5/game/ps5_triggers.h`. The car's speed, gear and nitro come from a new hook in the race HUD (`src/vehicle_telemetry.cpp`); the memory paths are from LARecomp, with credit.

NX2navi and Triforce have merged and go on as Triforce.

- This update turns NX2navi's launcher into the door to Triforce: one window that starts Triforce Setup, Triforce's
  launcher.
- Nothing of NX2navi is removed or changed: your built game, your saves and your settings stay where they are.
- **Play NX2navi** in that window still starts the game you have, for as long as you want it.
- Triforce builds the game from your own files, as NX2navi did, and its Convert saves page brings your NX2navi saves
  over.

## Good to know

- **Already have NX2navi:** the launcher updates itself to this version at its next check, as for any update. There is
  nothing to download by hand.
- **New here:** get Triforce from https://triforceproject.com. This release carries no setup.
- **What is no longer in the launcher:** its own pages for settings, mods, rebuilding the game, saves and Add to
  Steam. The game's own settings menu is unchanged.
- **Mods:** Play NX2navi starts the game as it is in its folder. A mod added after this update is not built in.
- **Steam:** a shortcut made with Add to Steam opens this window; choose Play NX2navi there.
- **Convert saves in Triforce v0.3.6** asks for the folder with your saves: it is the one the window shows as
  *Your NX2navi game and saves* (Copy path).
- **Uninstalling NX2navi** from Windows' Apps list works as before and asks before it removes the game folder.
- **Linux:** the AppImage has no updater and is not changed by this release.

The window's source is in [`handover/`](https://github.com/tangerineturtle1/NX2navi/tree/main/handover).

**IMPORTANT — Ocarina Reborn v1.1.4-1: PLEASE READ THE PATCH NOTES**

**🌲 New look**

**This is a small update on top of v1.1.4: a new launcher look, a new build screen, a new start screen and a portrait-mode camera fix. Engine, performance and memory behaviour are unchanged from v1.1.4.**

**🛠️ Launcher**
- New forest-themed launcher design with a new header, buttons and panels.
- The interface color you choose in the settings now tints the whole launcher.

**🔨 Build & update screen**
- Completely new build/update screen with a step list and one overall progress bar.
- Shows real progress and an accurate file counter (it no longer counts past the total).
- Steps an update does not need are shown as **not needed** instead of being ticked off.
- The build log can be opened directly from the screen.

**▶️ Start screen**
- New start screen after clicking **Play**, with three steps: **Check the launcher**, **Prepare the game** and **Start the game**, plus a real progress bar.

**📱 9:16 / portrait fix**
- On pictures narrower than 16:9 (for example **9:16**, 4:3 or 16:10), the gameplay camera now keeps the full 16:9 height view and shows more above and below instead of cutting off the sides.
- Cutscenes keep their own camera.

**ℹ️ Updating**
- **If you have v1.1.4 installed: download the installer from the website and install it over your existing version.** The launcher will not offer this update automatically because the main version number is unchanged.
- Let the launcher update the game once after installing.
- **No uninstall or game-file reimport is needed. Saves and settings stay.**

**📊 Help us improve**
- If you notice stutters, press **Ctrl+F8**, close the game and create a fresh **Debug Package**. After a crash, reopen the launcher to create it.
- Send it in **#post-your-logs-here** with the area and what happened. Reports from lower-end PCs are especially helpful.

Thanks for testing! 💙
